free.label: Free models
free.title:
Self-healing
free models.
free.intro: Free models die without notice. A curator probes them three times a day and rewrites the combo, so the free worker keeps answering.

dial.title: The curator clock
dial.caption: Default schedule (CURATOR_TIMES). The marker for the next run follows your local clock.
dial.svgLabel: A 24 hour dial with the three daily curator runs at 07:30, 13:30 and 19:30.

probe.title: The probe rule
probe.intro: Up to 14 candidates, two requests each, within the 40 req/min limit. A model stays in the combo only if all three hold.

items.d: A request with a get_time tool. OpenCode does not work without tool calling.

probe.outcome: The 4 best go into 9Router's database after a backup. If none pass, the combo is left alone and an alert is recorded.

items.what: 410 Gone: reached its end of life

incidents.why: 9Router does not skip to the next model on a 410 or 404, only on rate limits and server errors. One dead model at the top takes down every call.

security.label: Security
security.title:
Secrets never
leave the machine.
security.intro: Command-pattern filtering is decorative. Only the kernel holds the line, so the free worker runs inside one.

kernel.title: The kernel says no.
kernel.body: opencode-safe denies reads of .env files, keys, credentials, ~/.ssh and ~/.aws, whatever the command.
points: Windows: free worker off, use WSL2

hermes.title: No shell on chat.
hermes.body: A prompt injection cannot execute anything. Approvals are manual and only your ID can talk to the bot.

pinned.title: Pinned and audited.
pinned.body: Third-party tools install at reviewed versions, so a compromised upstream main never reaches your machine.

guard.title: Enforcement over instructions
guard.body: agent-model-guard is a hook that denies Opus subagents. Text rules do not work; enforcement does.

items.question: What is "smart vibe coding"?
items.answer: You steer intent and decisions; agents do the typing. "Smart" means spec first, cheap models for volume, independent review, verification before "done", and minimal tokens. See the [guide](docs/00-smart-vibe-coding.md).

items.question: How do I save tokens in Claude Code?
Can I use free models with Claude Code?
items.answer: Yes, as workers: OpenCode + 9Router with free NVIDIA NIM models. The curator keeps them healthy, and the sandbox makes sure they never see your secrets.

items.question: How do I run multiple Claude Code agents in parallel?
items.answer: Two ways: native subagents (`scout`/`builder`/`reviewer`) with worktree isolation, or alethe playbooks such as `parallel-worktrees` for Spec Kit `[P]` tasks.

items.question: Does it work with Codex, Gemini, Kiro or Copilot CLI?
items.answer: Codex is a native alethe provider (`WITH_CODEX=1`); the others plug in as custom workers. See [docs/04](docs/04-codex-and-other-clis.md).

items.question: Does it work on Windows?
items.answer: Yes for the core, workers, orchestration and schedules (PowerShell, Task Scheduler). The free-model worker needs a kernel sandbox, so on Windows run it under WSL2.

items.question: Will it delete or overwrite my files?
items.answer: No. It only appends blocks between `BEGIN/END` markers, merges JSON settings, and backs up every file it edits to `~/.local/share/agentic-dev-stack/backups/`. `uninstall` and `add-project --remove` take out only those blocks and entries.

items.question: Is it safe?
items.answer:
- Third-party pieces were audited and pinned to a reviewed version.
- The free worker is blocked from reading secrets at the kernel level.
- Hermes runs without a shell.
See [docs/07-security.md](docs/07-security.md).

cta.title:
Plan big,
execute small.
cta.line: Strong model for decisions, cheap model for volume.
cta.panelText: Stop running one AI agent at a time. The expensive model plans, cheap and free models execute, a reviewer from another provider checks the diff, and every turn spends the minimum number of tokens.
